page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an ARMv8 Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the single-core performance of the Neoverse-N1 processor is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1783.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1018.0. However, because of the single-core limitation, multi-core benchmarks are low, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 1017.0. Memory bandwidth is constrained, yielding 11.99 GB/sec for large block reads and 7.95 GB/sec for large block writes. Cryptographic performance is supported by hardware-accelerated AES instructions, though the architecture lacks AVX and AMX vector extensions.

This instance represents a cost-efficient entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, offering dedicated CPU resources at a low resource density. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads such as basic web serving, simple text processing, small-scale development environments, and testing ARM64 compatibility. It is not suitable for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded compilation, or high-throughput data processing.
